title: Managed environments: the framework's remaining local-password doors and copy (set-user-password on env_native rows, the platform-admin break-glass wording, the 'set a backup password' banner) contradict hosted's no-local-password rule
body:
repo:cloud#5 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjPP1zuWBNq3nBXVei9

Filing gate: ④ a child of the topic card objectstack-ai/cloud#4465, ruling 10 (hosted has no local break-glass admin; no local password for anyone), from the dev of objectstack-ai/cloud#4468 (PR objectstack-ai/cloud#4477).

## 维护者速读

托管上已经不允许任何人用本地密码登录。但框架里还有几处入口和提示仍在暗示可以设本地密码：
- 「给环境用户设密码」这个接口；
- 关于平台管理员应急密码的说明文字；
- 环境首页那条「设置备用密码」的横幅。

这些在托管上都应该关掉或不再显示。

## Work

On a managed (cloud-managed) environment:
- `plugin-auth` `cloud-managed.ts`: `CLOUD_MANAGED_REFUSAL_MESSAGES.setInitialPassword` / `setUserPassword` keep a platform-admin break-glass and `env_native` passwords. Refuse `set-user-password` on `env_native` rows too, and reword the messages so they promise no break-glass.
- The environment home's "set a backup password" banner (cloud#2430) is not shown.
- Self-hosted deployments are unchanged: they keep local admins.

The cloud already refuses password sign-in and its own `set-initial-password` twin on hosted (PR objectstack-ai/cloud#4477). This card aligns the framework's doors and copy, so nothing promises a password that hosted refuses.

`priority:p1` on the maintainer's word, verbatim: 「都是p1，车道自己认领就可以」. Triage routes it; the lane claims it.
